situation: Dilbert, wearing a bathrobe at work, is told by Alice that his attire marks him as a rebel and that he is now accepted into the group of cool rebels. In the final panel, a coworker standing nearby is shown continuing a bizarre wager about whether yellow is a flavor, with the loser getting a nail hammered into their skull.
punchline: The supposedly cool rebels turn out to be having a ridiculous argument that ends in a threat of violence, so being accepted into their group is far less appealing than it sounded.
summary: A woman welcomes a bathrobe-clad colleague into a gang of self-styled rebels whose idea of edgy conversation is a silly flavor debate with gruesome stakes.

title: Introducing the Little Stubborn Dumb Guy

transcript.speaker: Bob
transcript.text: I'd like you to meet the Little Stubborn Dumb Guy.

transcript.speaker: Bob
transcript.text: If for any reason I cannot fulfill my duty to thwart your project, the L.S.D.G. will take over for me.

transcript.speaker: Little Stubborn Dumb Guy
transcript.text: No, I won't.

transcript.speaker: Bob
transcript.text: Yes you will!!

situation: A man in a sweater introduces a miniature version of himself, the Little Stubborn Dumb Guy, to Dilbert. He explains that if he cannot obstruct Dilbert's project, the small guy will take over the obstruction. The little guy refuses to cooperate, and the big one angrily insists he will.
punchline: Even the designated backup saboteur is too stubborn to follow orders, so the stubbornness meant to thwart Dilbert ends up directed at his own boss.
summary: A project-blocking coworker presents his pint-sized stubborn understudy, who promptly refuses the job and gets shouted at.

file: 1999/1999-11-27_the turnaround ceo_turnaround is complete_new job_meat packing_reduce overhead_switch rooms_fisnih afternoon.gif
title: Turnaround CEO's Easy Next Job

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The Turnaround CEO

transcript.speaker: Turnaround CEO
transcript.text: The turnaround is complete. I'm off to my new job.

transcript.speaker: Turnaround CEO
transcript.text: It's a meat packing house that needs to reduce overhead.

transcript.speaker: Turnaround CEO
transcript.text: I figure I can switch a few room signs and finish in an afternoon.

setting: Office, with Dilbert holding a coffee mug beside a cubicle wall
situation: A red, horned devil-like figure introduced as the Turnaround CEO announces that he has finished his work at the company and is moving on to a new job. He explains the new employer is a meat packing house needing to cut overhead. He plans to simply swap a few room signs and be done in an afternoon, while Dilbert listens.
punchline: The CEO's cost-cutting method at a meat packer would be the same as his demonic corporate slaughter of jobs, requiring only new room signs, implying his layoffs are essentially butchery.
summary: A demonic corporate hatchet man brags that his next gig at a slaughterhouse will need barely any adjustment from his usual downsizing routine.

title: Manager's Expensive 900 Number Call

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Our profits were good until a manager ...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: ... used his credit card to make a 900 call from an airplane phone.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Hey, I'm allowed to call my wife when I'm traveling!

situation: Dilbert presents a profit chart to managers at a meeting table, explaining that profits were good until a manager charged a 900 call from an airplane phone to his credit card. One of the managers, with pointy hair, immediately and defensively speaks up, giving himself away.
punchline: The manager inadvertently confesses by defensively claiming he was only calling his wife, since 900 numbers are premium-rate services, usually adult lines, so the excuse is absurd and incriminating.
summary: A presenter blames a manager's costly airline phone call for lost profits, and a guilty-looking executive in the audience blurts out a laughable excuse.

file: 1999/1999-08-25_bog stubborn_dumb guy_contract employees_email_bulletin list_incremental cost_agree with me_our lives.gif
title: Big Stubborn Dumb Guy Fights Logic

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Big Stubborn Dumb Guy

transcript.speaker: Big Stubborn Dumb Guy
transcript.text: We should remove the contract employees from our e-mail bulletin list.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Um... They need that information to do their jobs, and there's no incremental cost.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: This is when you agree with me and we move on with our lives.

transcript.speaker: Big Stubborn Dumb Guy
transcript.text: I will fight you to the end of the earth!

situation: At a meeting, a coworker labeled Big Stubborn Dumb Guy proposes removing contract employees from the e-mail bulletin list. Dilbert calmly points out that they need the information to do their jobs and that keeping them on costs nothing extra. Rather than concede, the stubborn coworker vows to fight him to the end of the earth.
punchline: A stubborn person will defend a pointless, counterproductive position with absurd intensity even after being shown it makes no sense, so reasonable people can't simply resolve it and move on.
summary: A coworker who refuses to back down over a pointless cost-cutting idea turns a simple, sensible objection into an endless battle.
keywords: fight to the end of the earth

title: No Innocent Employees Will Be Hired

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Your project is to build a call center to handle customer questions.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Keep the costs down by making the working conditions inhumane.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My conscience won't allow me to harm innocent employees.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: We won't be paying enough to hire any innocent employees.

situation: The Boss assigns Dilbert to build a customer call center and tells him to cut costs by making working conditions inhumane. Dilbert objects that his conscience won't let him harm innocent employees. The Boss replies that the low pay means only non-innocent people will take the jobs.
punchline: The Boss dismisses Dilbert's ethical objection by implying that the pay will be so poor that only guilty people would apply, so no innocent employees will ever be harmed.
summary: A manager shrugs off an engineer's moral qualms about miserable call center conditions by arguing the wages will only attract people who deserve it.

file: 1999/1999-02-16_cat bert_hr dorector_nput of employees_morons_sing loudly_thinking_pinball wizard.gif
title: Catbert Ignores Morons By Singing

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Catbert: H.R. Director

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: I value the input of all employees...

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: ...including the morons. Although in those cases, I cover my ears and sing loudly.

transcript.speaker: Employee
transcript.text: So I was thinking maybe...

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: He's a pinball wizard

situation: Catbert, the H.R. Director, sits on his desk and tells an employee that he values everyone's input. He admits that when the input comes from morons, he covers his ears and sings loudly. When the employee starts to share an idea, Catbert demonstrates by covering his ears and singing a pinball song.
punchline: Catbert's claim to value all employee input is a sham, since he literally drowns out any employee he considers a moron, and he treats this one as one of them.
summary: A feline human resources chief explains how he blocks out the suggestions of employees he deems foolish, then promptly does it to the staffer standing in front of him.

title: Flossing Despite Coworker's Disgust

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Do you mind if I floss?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Yes. I would be thoroughly disgusted and hate you forever.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Well, I can't please everyone.

situation: A dark-haired coworker seated at a table with Dilbert asks whether Dilbert minds if he flosses his teeth. Dilbert honestly replies that he would be disgusted and hate the coworker forever. The coworker shrugs it off and flosses anyway while Dilbert glares.
punchline: The coworker asks permission as a mere courtesy, and when given an honest objection he ignores it and does what he wanted, using 'I can't please everyone' as an excuse.
summary: A man politely asks to floss in front of Dilbert, hears a blunt refusal, and proceeds to do it regardless.

title: Venture Capital Funds Lazy Dishonest Startup

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Venture capitalists gave me money to start a web-based business.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Do they know you're lazy and dishonest?

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: It didn't come up.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What'll you create... besides accounting irregularities?

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: That's all I have the energy for.

situation: Wally walks up to Dilbert carrying a big sack of money and announces that venture capitalists funded his new web-based business. Dilbert asks whether the investors know Wally is lazy and dishonest, and Wally says it never came up. Dilbert then asks what he will actually create, and Wally admits he only has the energy for accounting irregularities.
punchline: Wally got investor money without anyone vetting his character, and he cheerfully admits the only thing his laziness will let him produce is creative bookkeeping fraud.
summary: A notoriously idle coworker lands a pile of startup cash and cheerfully concedes that fudging the books is the extent of his ambition.

file: 1999/1999-05-21_attached tracking device_compromise_spy satellite_radio network_next weekend_date tried to run_nod once.gif
title: Dilbert Stalks His Date Electronically

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My date tried to run away, but I attached a tracking device to her coat.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Now I'll just compromise a spy satellite and a radio network.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: ...So, if next weekend is good, nod once.

setting: Dilbert's home, then the date's bedroom at night
situation: Dilbert explains that his date tried to flee, so he planted a tracking device on her coat. He then hijacks a spy satellite and a radio network to reach her. In the last panel, his voice booms from a radio on her nightstand while she lies in bed looking unimpressed, as he asks her to nod once if next weekend is good.
punchline: Dilbert's elaborate high-tech stalking is wildly creepy, yet he treats it as a normal way to arrange a second date.
summary: A lovelorn engineer bugs his date's coat and hacks into satellites just to ask her out again from a speaker beside her bed.

file: 1999/1999-03-09_boss acts bull_fast_pointy haired_rodeo clown_woo hoo_taunts boss_employee_new hire.gif
title: The New Guy Taunts the Boss

transcript.speaker: New Employee
transcript.text: Wah-wah! Woo-hoo!

transcript.speaker: New Employee
transcript.text: Yee-ha!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Snort.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Just as I suspected, the new guy is a rodeo clown.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: He's fast.

situation: A new employee waves his arms and taunts the Pointy-Haired Boss, who snorts and charges like an angry bull. The new guy vaults over a cubicle wall to escape. Dilbert and Wally watch from their cubicles and conclude the new hire must be a rodeo clown.
punchline: The Boss behaves so much like a bull that the new employee instinctively treats him like one, and his agile dodging reveals he is a rodeo clown.
summary: A newcomer teases the boss like a charging bull and leaps over a cubicle wall to escape, revealing his rodeo background to the amused coworkers.

title: Customer Appreciation Theme: Many Idiots

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Asok, you've been chosen to head our customer appreciation celebration.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: The theme is "Thank goodness there are so many idiots."

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: When do you plan to tell him it's a joke?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Let's see how the posters turn out.

situation: Alice tells the young intern Asok he has been put in charge of the customer appreciation celebration, then hands him an insulting theme about customers being idiots. At lunch, Dilbert asks when she plans to tell Asok it's a joke, and Alice says she'll wait to see how the posters turn out.
punchline: Alice is deliberately letting naive Asok produce posters insulting customers for her own amusement, with no intention of stopping him until the damage is visible.
summary: A cynical coworker assigns the gullible intern an insulting slogan for a client celebration and happily lets him run with it as a prank.

title: Angry Caller Reaches Designer's Mother

transcript.speaker: Elderly Woman
transcript.text: Hello. May I speak to the moron who designed my computer?

transcript.speaker: Elderly Woman
transcript.text: My computer locks up five times a day. I'm going to drive over to your house and kick your white, pimply...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Hi, Mom.

transcript.speaker: Elderly Woman
transcript.text: Oh, I'll find it!

setting: A home, with a computer on a desk
situation: An elderly woman phones the company that made her computer and demands to speak to the moron who designed it. She threatens to drive to his house and kick his white, pimply backside because her machine locks up five times a day. The designer who comes on the line turns out to be Dilbert, and she is his mother.
punchline: The angry caller has unknowingly insulted and threatened her own son, and her sudden cheerful switch to maternal mode ('Oh, I'll find it!') shows she is retrieving his usual things rather than actually following through.
summary: A furious customer's rant about faulty hardware goes awry when the engineer on the other end is her own child.

file: 1999/1999-11-03_designing call center_eployees_bathroom breaks_tiny cubicles_monitor calls_speed_customer service.gif
title: Collecting Abuser Requirements for Call Center

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Designing a call center

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Give the employees six minutes of bathroom breaks per shift.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Tiny cubicles... and we'll monitor calls and have incompatible objectives, such as speed and customer service.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: How's the project going?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm still collecting the abuser requirements.

situation: Dilbert takes notes while Catbert and the Boss dictate cruel design features for a call center: minimal bathroom breaks, tiny cubicles, call monitoring and contradictory goals. Later, Wally asks Dilbert how the project is going.
punchline: Dilbert reframes the standard 'user requirements' phase as 'abuser requirements', since the call center is being designed to mistreat its own employees.
summary: A call center is engineered around employee misery, so the requirements gathering is really a list of ways to mistreat the staff.

file: 1999/1999-07-18_feng shui consultant_one in your vent_rubber bands_spirits_trousers_evil soirits_koi pond_feel any luckier.gif
title: Feng Shui Consultant Scares Boss Silly

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The Feng Shui Consultant

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: This office is swarming with evil spirits.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: It is?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: There's one in your vent!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Ooh — he ducked back in before you saw him.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Put rubber bands around your pant legs to keep the spirits out of your trousers.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I figure the evil spirits will mount a rear assault through that window.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Aaagh!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: It's gone now.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: What did you see?!!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Your only hope is to turn your secretary's cubicle into a koi pond.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Do you feel any luckier?

setting: The Boss's office and an adjacent cubicle
situation: Dogbert, posing as a feng shui consultant, convinces the Boss that his office is full of evil spirits. He escalates with absurd, scary remedies like rubber bands around the Boss's pant legs and a fake sighting through the window. His final prescription is to flood the secretary's cubicle into a koi pond, leaving her sitting in water in snorkel gear.
punchline: Dogbert exploits the Boss's gullibility to pile on ridiculous demands, and the only person who suffers is the secretary, soaked in a koi pond while Dilbert asks if she feels luckier.
summary: A pet-turned-consultant frightens his gullible client with imaginary demons until the staff ends up swimming in a fish pond.

title: Teflon Spray Ignores Subordinates' Input

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dogbert consults

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Spray this Teflon(TM) on your body to better ignore the input of your subordinates.

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: Sploit!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Next time, shake well before using.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Who cares what you say?!

setting: The Boss's office, with Dogbert sitting on his desk
situation: Dogbert, acting as a consultant, sells the Boss a can of Teflon spray that supposedly helps him ignore his subordinates' input. The Boss sprays it, the can sputters and splatters, and Dogbert advises him to shake it well next time. The Boss, now seemingly coated in the stuff, brushes off the advice with 'Who cares what you say?!'
punchline: The Boss's dismissive reply to Dogbert's advice shows the spray already works, so he now ignores everyone's input, including the consultant who sold it to him.
summary: A consultant dog hawks a non-stick spray that lets a manager shrug off employee feedback, and the manager promptly shrugs off the dog's usage tips.

file: 1999/1999-04-27_budget numbers_totally inaccurate_only numbers_infinite inaccurate numbers_encrypt them.gif
title: Infinite Inaccurate Budget Numbers

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Do you have those budget numbers from last month?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: They're totally inaccurate.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I know, but those are the only numbers we have.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Actually, we have infinite inaccurate numbers to choose from.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Let's keep those in our back pocket in case we need them.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'll encrypt them so no one else can use them.

situation: The Boss asks Dilbert for last month's budget numbers, and Dilbert admits they are totally inaccurate. The Boss insists they are the only numbers available, so Dilbert points out that any number could be invented. The Boss wants to keep the bad figures in reserve, and Dilbert offers to encrypt them.
punchline: Dilbert sarcastically treats worthless, made-up budget figures as valuable secrets worth encrypting, mocking the idea of hoarding bad data.
summary: A manager wants to stash faulty financial figures for later, and his employee deadpans by offering to lock them up with encryption.

title: Faking Equality While Talking Down

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'll come around the desk so it appears that I consider you an equal.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: So, what's on your little mind?

situation: The Boss sits behind his desk while an employee (resembling Wally) stands before him holding papers. The Boss announces he will come around the desk to create the appearance of treating the employee as an equal. He moves his chair around the desk, then lounges back and condescendingly asks what is on the employee's 'little mind'.
punchline: The Boss openly admits his gesture of equality is just for show, and then immediately undermines it by patronizingly calling the employee's mind 'little'.
summary: A manager stages a show of friendliness by moving around his desk, then ruins it with a condescending question.

file: 1999/1999-09-14_too underfunded_succeed_slow day_slide toward failure_moms unconditional love_hold me to that.gif
title: Mom's Unconditional Love Fallback

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm working on a project that is too under-funded to succeed.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Every day is a slow but inevitable slide toward failure and humiliation.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: At least I'll always have my mom's unconditional love.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Mom
transcript.text: Are you going to hold me to that?

situation: Dilbert holds a cup of coffee in the kitchen while his mom chops carrots, and he complains that his project is too under-funded to succeed and each day is a slide toward failure and humiliation. He consoles himself that he will always have his mother's unconditional love. His mom responds by asking whether he is going to hold her to that.
punchline: Dilbert's mom hints that her unconditional love may not be as guaranteed as he assumes, undercutting his only source of comfort.
summary: Dilbert wallows over a doomed, starved-of-money project and finds solace in his mother's love, only for her to question whether that love is a promise.

file: 1999/1999-03-08_boss can't understand hire_rodeo clown_engineer_smells like hay_fifty percent_data network engineer_engineering.gif
title: Boss Hires Rodeo Clown Maybe

transcript.speaker: Job Candidate
transcript.text: Mwa fwa fwa ooh mah fuh.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I can't understand a word you say.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: And you're poorly dressed. You must be some sort of technology expert.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Or a rodeo clown.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: There's a fifty percent chance I hired a data network engineer.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: I smell hay.

situation: The Boss interviews a candidate who speaks gibberish and wears shabby, patched clothes. Unable to understand him and judging only by his appearance, the Boss concludes he is either a technology expert or a rodeo clown, then hires him anyway. A colleague nearby notices a smell of hay.
punchline: The Boss hires on appearance and incomprehensibility alone, so there is a real chance the new hire is a rodeo clown, as the hay smell suggests, rather than an engineer.
summary: A manager hires an unintelligible, scruffy applicant on a coin-flip guess about his profession, and a coworker's sniff test hints it went badly.
